title: Dems re-up overtime bill that would set threshold over $89K by 2030
summary: Following the U.S. Department of Labor’s overtime rule rescission, Congressional Democrats introduced a bill that would greatly expand the number of workers who qualify for overtime.

title: This week in 5 numbers: More than 1 in 5 employees say they’ve witnessed unethical or illegal conduct at work
summary: Here’s a roundup of numbers from the last week of HR news — including how many women hold seats on the corporate boards of Russell 3000 companies.

title: 7 stories on the state of pay in the workplace
summary: The standard 3% to 5% annual raise has lost its advantage, a recent analysis suggests.

title: Amid daunting constraints, companies say they remain committed to inclusion
summary: However, federal contractors have faced regulatory pressure, prompting the majority to decrease inclusion efforts, per a report.

title: Burnout is increasing, while employee confidence is at a record low, research shows
summary: Worker burnout happens when employees “face a chronic, unmanageable amount” of stress, a senior economist for Glassdoor said.

title: Target leadership under fire over ‘strategic missteps’ on DEI, ICE
summary: Earlier this year, Target came under fire for its restrained response to two of its employees being detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents at one of its locations in Minneapolis.

title: Feds, home care company eye $3M deal to end overtime, misclassification claims
summary: The lawsuit stemmed from a U.S. Department of Labor investigation allegedly finding that employees were intentionally misclassified as independent contractors.

title: Women’s representation is slipping on corporate boards
summary: President Donald Trump’s top-down attack on diversity and inclusion has trickled into every aspect of work.

title: Indeed parent company touts record growth driven by AI
summary: Despite ongoing concerns about artificial intelligence disrupting job boards, Indeed posted record high users in March, Recruit Holdings said.

title: Employer to pay $4.25M to settle claims it failed to consider vaccine exemptions
summary: Recent EEOC enforcement involving COVID-19 vaccines appears to go hand in hand with the administration’s broader prioritization of Christian issues.
